releaseScope: Native Rust/GPUI preview for Arch/Omarchy Linux x86_64
releaseState: Source preview; public binary release is not qualified

statusDefinitions.label: Locally tested
statusDefinitions.meaning: The named bounded journey passed on this development host. It is not a portability or universal quality claim.

statusDefinitions.label: Implemented / needs qualification
statusDefinitions.meaning: The source and UI path exist, but the current change or broader real-world claim still needs its final evidence.

statusDefinitions.label: Experimental
statusDefinitions.meaning: Available only through a bounded preview, explicit Try path, or provider-specific evidence.

statusDefinitions.label: Planned
statusDefinitions.meaning: Documented product direction without an implemented, qualified release path.

statusDefinitions.label: Blocked / deferred / excluded
statusDefinitions.meaning: Waiting on external evidence or deliberately outside the current preview scope.

releaseSnapshot.label: Current regression suite
releaseSnapshot.detail: 326 library, 179 UI and 229 integration tests; all 80 templates and the Create exports passed. Production Wayland/XWayland and the matching installed preview also passed.

releaseSnapshot.label: Large-photo Create editing
releaseSnapshot.detail: Three paired desktop repetitions: paint core 85.69 → 0.32 ms; headless frame/refresh 257.88 → 165.38 ms. Recovery idle before each stroke; exact undo/redo/recovery, unchanged peak memory. Physical input latency remains unmeasured.

releaseSnapshot.label: Public-release blockers
releaseSnapshot.detail: Two dependency texts, remote CI/GitHub App connection, clean installation and physical desktop acceptance remain open.

categories.name: Photo editing
categories.summary: Ordinary raster work is broad and locally exercised; the active release pass is tightening real-photo colour, precision and scale evidence.

items.name: Core raster editing
items.current: Brush, Pencil, Eraser, Fill, Gradient, Crop, Resize, Move, Clone, Blur, Smudge, Liquify, Heal, Spot Heal and destructive filters are wired into the native editor with undo/redo.
items.boundary: Bounded local journeys do not establish every brush size, transform, colour space or long-session workload.

items.name: Selections and selection-aware edits
items.current: Marquee, ellipse, lasso, wand, object selection, feathered coverage and selection-aware filters/content fill are implemented; the hardened paths preserve soft coverage and undo.
items.boundary: Quality still depends on the source and tool settings; physical input delivery is a separate desktop gate.

items.name: Retouching and controlled removal
items.current: Healing layers, clone/heal tools, frequency separation, dodge/burn, refinement and controlled removal have bounded native and regression evidence.
items.boundary: Healing strokes are raster edits rather than replayable source-linked recipes; broad portrait and object-removal quality review remains separate.

items.name: Adjustments, filters and editable stacks
items.current: Exposure, levels, curves, hue/saturation, colour balance, blur, sharpen, denoise, grain/noise, vignette, bloom, tonal contrast, invert and grayscale are available through destructive and editable paths.
items.boundary: The Camera Raw compatibility node remains an 8-bit path; not every traditional adjustment/effect can be exported at full precision.

items.name: Embedded RAW development
items.current: LibRaw import retains original bytes and a 16-bit editable source. After visual review rejected a grossly magenta result, the corrected Nikon and Canon outputs both match the independent C++ camera-white-balance PPM16 references exactly for every retained sample and were visually inspected as natural.
items.boundary: The earlier two-camera evidence uses the same pinned LibRaw engine, not an independent audit of LibRaw colour science or a general camera-colour claim. The current 734-test suite passed with the Nikon RAW fixture enabled; the full 16-case corpus was not repeated for the history/ownership changes.

items.name: Real-photo and large-document qualification
items.current: The 16 photo cases passed at ac8874d. The isolated region-history workload at a69a5f6 passed 18 runs with 100 strokes, exact final undo/redo pixels, .omuse save/reopen and PNG export; routine medians were 2.00/2.13/0.42 ms at 12/24/48 MP. The later desktop ownership comparison is recorded separately below.
items.boundary: The earlier isolated editor fixture measured median peak RSS of 326/610/1200 MiB and does not establish physical input latency. The later desktop fixture also waits for recovery before painting. Rapid strokes during background work, native large-camera decode and long sessions still need qualification.

items.name: Region/tile-based large-photo history
items.current: Large unselected Brush, Pencil and Eraser strokes retain reversible 256×256 tiles. Current differential regressions pass. Historical a69a5f6 measurements retained 100 undo steps at 48 MP using about 30.96 MiB of final history, compared with one step before.
items.boundary: Masks, selected strokes, clone/heal and other transactions keep snapshots. Persistent Create raster owners are now removed, but recovery, collection checkpoints and saves can still force copies. The earlier 12/24 MP first strokes were slower; neither workload qualifies whole-app input latency.

items.name: Large-photo desktop page ownership
items.current: Editors own active and cached page pixels; complete save/export/recovery snapshots remain frozen. All 18 paired cases passed. At 48 MP, paint core measured 85.69 → 0.32 ms and headless frame/refresh 257.88 → 165.38 ms. Editing during a same-path save can recover, export and save again.
items.boundary: Twelve localized strokes after a warmup, three repetitions per strategy/size; recovery idle before each measured stroke. Peak RSS was essentially unchanged. In-flight snapshots can still force full copies, and end-of-stroke refresh has large outliers. These are not physical input timings.

categories.name: Layers and masks
categories.summary: The native document model covers hierarchy, editable effects and multiple mask types with bounded persistence and transaction tests.

items.name: Layer hierarchy and compositing
items.current: Pixel layers, groups, transforms, opacity, blend modes, clipping, visibility, locking, reorder/copy and grouped editing are implemented.
items.boundary: Cross-window layer drops and complete parity with every legacy Mac gesture remain outside the current evidence.

items.name: Raster, linked and folder masks
items.current: Per-layer masks, detached placement, link/unlink behavior, live alpha links and folder masks persist through project save/reopen.
items.boundary: Mask rasterization and document limits remain bounded; older project versions cannot represent every newer mask feature.

items.name: Adjustment layers and layer effects
items.current: Hue/Saturation, Levels, Curves, Exposure, Gradient Map and Grain adjustment records coexist with stroke, shadows, colour overlay and outer glow effects.
items.boundary: Legacy-reader support varies by project version, and 16-bit export rejects unsupported traditional adjustment/effect records rather than flattening silently.

items.name: Editable filter stacks and Blend If
items.current: Retained sources support ordered filter nodes, opacity, selection masks and backdrop-aware Blend If with channel controls.
items.boundary: Editable layers are capped at 128 nodes; source and mask storage budgets apply, and evaluation remains CPU-heavy for large images.

items.name: Range masks and edge refinement
items.current: Luminosity/colour ranges can replace, add or subtract selections or produce layer masks; refinement supports correction strokes, edge controls and multiple inspection backgrounds.
items.boundary: Range parameters are not persisted as a live parametric mask recipe, and refined cut-outs bake the correction result.

items.name: Vector masks
items.current: Cubic path geometry remains editable while its vector mask is rasterized into layer coverage; path Apply rebuilds that coverage transactionally.
items.boundary: This is a bounded path/mask workflow, not compound-path boolean authoring or a complete vector illustration system.

categories.name: Vector, type and design
categories.summary: Live type, shape and layout objects now support native branded design while preserving an explicit boundary around full illustration tooling.

items.name: Live text and rich typography
items.current: Editable text supports rich runs, alignment, fitting, minimum sizes, reusable styles, text backgrounds and overflow reports.
items.boundary: Unusual fallback fonts, long copy, manual rich-run editing and assistive workflows remain manual release checks.

items.name: Live shapes and paths
items.current: Rectangles, rounded rectangles, ellipses, lines and editable cubic paths retain style/geometry until deliberately rasterized.
items.boundary: Boolean operations, compound paths and variable-width strokes are not implemented as a general illustration suite.

items.name: Frames and collages
items.current: Replaceable image frames retain crop placement, focal point, rounded boundary and nondestructive replacement metadata.
items.boundary: Frame/cutout visual quality across arbitrary source photography remains a manual review area.

items.name: Brand kits and editable templates
items.current: Brand colours, logos, font pairs, text styles and spacing rules feed 20 native templates and 80 qualified variants.
items.boundary: The completed variants are bounded fixtures; arbitrary user brands and missing-font substitutions require manual review.

items.name: Responsive layout and resizing
items.current: Alignment, distribution, anchoring and aspect-ratio adaptation retain live text/shapes and editable overrides.
items.boundary: Layout preflight is conservative and does not judge every image backdrop, rich text run or destination safe area.

items.name: Reusable components and shared backgrounds
items.current: Reusable logos, badges, footers and calls to action support bounded instance overrides and explicit propagation across pages.
items.boundary: Components are project-native structures, not a remote collaborative design-system service.

items.name: Mesh and pin deformation
items.current: A retained 2×2 corner mesh and bounded pin warp can be previewed, applied, reopened and adjusted.
items.boundary: The UI is not a general mesh-grid editor; evaluation is CPU-based and capped at 16 MP.

categories.name: Create and social content
categories.summary: Create is implemented as a native content-production workspace for editable assets and export, without scheduling or social account management.

items.name: Pages, artboards and carousels
items.current: `.omuse` collections support mixed page sizes, page strips, reorder/duplicate, shared backgrounds, numbering and collection undo/redo.
items.boundary: Older application builds may not understand Create metadata; keep the full collection package intact.

items.name: Phone preview, guides and content packs
items.current: Phone preview, composition guides and staged export produce ordered PNG/JPEG/WebP pages, multipage PDF, captions, alt text and a manifest.
items.boundary: Safe-area guidance is conservative; destination applications can crop or overlay content differently.

items.name: CSV bulk creation
items.current: CSV rows bind typed text, image, visibility and alt fields to approved templates with validation, preview and meaningful output names.
items.boundary: A representative user batch, row-error presentation and final naming review remain manual acceptance work.

items.name: Local asset library
items.current: Local photos, cutouts, logos, backgrounds and saved compositions can be searched, tagged, favourited and packaged into projects with provenance.
items.boundary: This is a local library; cloud sync and collaborative asset governance are not claimed.

items.name: Motion and animated output
items.current: Page/layer fades, rise, slow pan, durations, transitions and local MP4/GIF export are implemented through FFmpeg.
items.boundary: FFmpeg availability and user-media compatibility remain host-dependent; a saved assistant animation plan was not separately rendered in its live AI journey.

items.name: Short clips, audio and subtitles
items.current: Supplied clips can be probed, trimmed and split; projects retain audio settings and editable SRT/WebVTT cues for soft or burned subtitles.
items.boundary: Cancellation, unusual codecs and a broad user-media matrix remain release checks.

items.name: Automatic transcription
items.current: Subtitle import and editing exist; automatic transcription is documented as a future, separately qualified capability.
items.boundary: There is no current transcription runtime or release claim.

items.name: Calendars, scheduling and publishing
items.current: Explicitly excluded from Omuse's product scope. Content sets may have names, briefs and versions without dates, publishing states or analytics.
items.boundary: This is an exclusion, not an unfinished preview promise.

categories.name: AI
categories.summary: Omuse keeps AI inside staged, reviewable document transactions; only a narrow Codex subscription journey has bounded live evidence.

items.name: Ask Omuse job, review and history model
items.current: Provider routes, billing labels, Local-only mode, bounded jobs, review groups, stale-result protection, Keep, Undo and saved provenance are implemented.
items.boundary: A local invariant does not prove provider availability, visual quality or cancellation after remote acceptance.

items.name: Codex subscription route
items.current: A signed-in Codex CLI route passed bounded restoration of one Generate result, one new protected-subject Background edit and one six-page native design-assistant carousel.
items.boundary: This does not qualify every account, runtime version, prompt, image operation or general provider support.

items.name: Generate and image-edit operations
items.current: Generate, selection replacement, background edit, canvas expansion, removal, references, variations and refinement have source/UI paths.
items.boundary: Replacement, expansion, removal, multi-variation cancellation and broader failure/restart cases still need live receipts before support claims.

items.name: Native design assistant
items.current: Design with me and Improve layout can propose bounded native plans that select pages, place packaged resources and instantiate components with overrides.
items.boundary: Only the named Codex carousel has live evidence; arbitrary provider plans and assistant-led resizing need their own qualification.

items.name: Caption and alt-text drafting
items.current: The assistant can stage caption and alt-text drafts for explicit review before keeping them in export metadata.
items.boundary: Standalone caption drafting still needs a bounded live provider receipt and human content review.

items.name: Local product finishing
items.current: Protected-subject background results can receive undoable local soft/contact shadow and subtle reflection layers without sending those choices to a provider.
items.boundary: The source/UI path and local regression checks pass; the final visual quality of product shadows/reflections still needs a representative human review.

items.name: Claude and Grok subscription routes
items.current: Adapters exist. The recorded qualification found Claude signed out; Grok's official runtime identity, account state and isolated operation remain unverified.
items.boundary: Neither route should be advertised as supported until official sign-in, capability and in-app operation receipts exist.

items.name: Direct API routes
items.current: Optional separately billed API access remains disabled pending an explicit key and billing-route decision.
items.boundary: Omuse must never switch from subscription access to separately billed API use silently.

categories.name: Formats and colour
categories.summary: Omuse preserves editable project state and common raster/media outputs while keeping colour and format limitations explicit.

items.name: `.comp` projects
items.current: The Rust reader/writer covers project versions 1–7: canvas, hierarchy, transforms, opacity/blends, raster/live/folder masks and adjustment layers.
items.boundary: Newer Rust-specific editable assets may render only as cached images in preserved older editors and may not survive resave there.

items.name: `.omuse` collections
items.current: Multi-page native collections retain pages, resources, brand/components, Create history, motion and export metadata through save/reopen and recovery.
items.boundary: This is the active native format; cross-version and independent macOS interchange still need broader external review.

items.name: Raster import and export
items.current: PNG, JPEG, TIFF, WebP and common image import paths support orientation, tagged colour conversion, staged publication and explicit JPEG matte/quality behavior.
items.boundary: The 14 non-RAW corpus cases and current Rust/UI regressions pass, including warning-free TIFF alpha decoding. Broader format and clean-machine qualification remain separate.

items.name: PSD subset
items.current: Flattened 8-bit RGB PSDs with Raw, PackBits, ZIP or ZIP prediction open as editable merged images; malformed and unsupported modes are rejected.
items.boundary: Tagged PSD colour management and complete layered PSD parity are not supported; embedded ICC profiles currently trigger conversion guidance.

items.name: ICC and working spaces
items.current: ICC-tagged imports normalize through LittleCMS; editable sources can use sRGB, Linear sRGB or Display P3, and software display proofing exposes intents and black-point compensation.
items.boundary: End-to-end wide-gamut compositing/export, calibrated monitor validation, compositor colour management, HDR display and print-proof accuracy are unqualified.

items.name: Retained 16-bit precision and export
items.current: High-bit-depth PNG/TIFF and RAW sources retain non-quantized 16-bit masters for editable processing and explicit 16-bit PNG/TIFF export.
items.boundary: Both RAW references and retained/explicit PNG/TIFF samples pass exact 16-bit comparison; high-precision sources remain capped at 16,777,216 pixels. Standard export is 8-bit, while explicit PNG/TIFF export is 16-bit. Ordinary destructive painting requires an explicit conversion to 8-bit pixels.

items.name: Persistent 32-bit HDR workflow
items.current: Not implemented as a persistent document or export mode.
items.boundary: Existing HDR merge and P3 working-space features must not be described as a 32-bit floating-point HDR pipeline.

categories.name: Linux experience
categories.summary: The current product is a native GPUI/Omarchy application with strong local journeys and unresolved physical-device and portability gates.

items.name: Native GPUI/Omarchy interface
items.current: The Studio shell, tool dock, Layers, Develop, Selection, Canvas, Create and Assistant inspectors, themes, dialogs and native canvas are implemented in Rust/GPUI.
items.boundary: This is the active native app, distinct from the historical Swift/Qt Linux port and its older parity reports.

items.name: Wayland and XWayland journeys
items.current: Production and installed-preview windows passed bounded native Wayland/XWayland editing journeys, including an 800×600 GPUI viewport and light/dark/reduced-motion checks.
items.boundary: These journeys dispatch GPUI events in process and do not prove compositor-delivered physical input.

items.name: Isolated preview installation
items.current: The current production build passed Wayland and minimum-window XWayland journeys. The installed omuse-preview has the identical executable hash and passed its editing self-test from /tmp; both previous preview versions are preserved.
items.boundary: A development-host install is not a clean-machine package or a portable Linux binary.

items.name: Physical keyboard, pointer and Cua
items.current: The Omarchy-specific Cua path captured the exact app window in a disposable nested session, but foreground pointer/keyboard injection was refused. The main desktop plugin is inactive until a fresh desktop session.
items.boundary: No physical-input pass is claimed. Real foreground keyboard/pointer, clipboard and file-dialog acceptance remain release gates.

items.name: Tablet pressure and tilt
items.current: Wayland tablet-v2 pressure, tilt, tool identity and proximity events are wired, but physical tablet support is deferred for this preview.
items.boundary: Synthetic backend tests do not establish device mapping, driver behavior or X11 pressure/tilt.

items.name: Displays, DPI and accessibility
items.current: Minimum-window layouts, themes, reduced motion and bounded scale behavior have automated/native coverage.
items.boundary: Real mixed-DPI/multi-monitor behavior, physical trackpad input and AT-SPI exact-window coverage remain unqualified.

items.name: Distribution portability
items.current: The preview targets this Arch/Omarchy x86_64 host and glibc 2.44. Omuse-native packaging/AppStream and clean supported-system installation are still pending.
items.boundary: The tracked legacy Compositor Flatpak material is not an Omuse distribution package.

categories.name: Reliability and release
categories.summary: Transaction, recovery and bounds work is substantial, while public distribution still depends on current qualification and external release infrastructure.

items.name: Undo, async work and publication safety
items.current: Document transactions, undo/redo, stale-result rejection, cancellable background open/export/save and staged publication guard against partial or late results.
items.boundary: Cancellation cannot retract work already accepted by an external provider, and not every long-running workload has soak evidence.

items.name: Save, recovery and interruption
items.current: Staged saves, external identity checks and isolated recovery preserve complete packages. The current suite also covers older lazy snapshots and newer edits across same-path background saves. Earlier multi-revision SIGKILL qualification remains recorded separately.
items.boundary: Process interruption is not sudden power-loss durability; a clean filesystem and machine matrix remains untested.

items.name: Resource and untrusted-input bounds
items.current: Decoder, PSD, AI response, media probe, CSV/bulk, document and editable-source limits fail explicitly instead of silently overcommitting.
items.boundary: A focused security and supply-chain review of untrusted imports and provider boundaries remains a public-release gate.

items.name: Current candidate regression suite
items.current: The current changes passed 734 Rust tests: 326 library, 179 UI and 229 integration tests. The editing journey, six-page PNG/PDF/MP4/GIF exports, 80 editable templates, production Wayland/XWayland and matching installed-preview self-test also passed.
items.boundary: Four manual timing benchmarks were excluded from the regression gate; the desktop comparison ran separately and passed all 18 cases. Local checks do not replace clean public-repository CI or broader hardware and live-provider acceptance.

items.name: Dependency notice gate
items.current: Exact upstream texts were recovered for `seahash` and `simd_helpers`; `hexf-parse 0.2.1` and `mac 0.1.1` remain unresolved.
items.boundary: The two missing legal texts keep the public-binary notice gate open; generic licence boilerplate is intentionally rejected.

items.name: Remote CI and GitHub App connection
items.current: Rust workflow definitions exist, but the first clean public-repository run is pending and the GitHub App connection needed to operate that path is missing in the current session.
items.boundary: Local tests and workflow files do not prove a green remote run for the exact release candidate.

items.name: Clean install and release identity
items.current: The production and installed executable hashes match, native checks pass, and rollback copies are retained. A source-only public snapshot is prepared separately; a clean binary release/tag and clean target installation remain pending.
items.boundary: No downloadable public preview should be claimed until that exact artifact path is reproduced on a clean supported system.

items.name: Security, support and supply chain
items.current: Contribution and bug-report entry points exist; vulnerability reporting, owner-approved security policy, maintenance scope, dependency vulnerability review and signing/attestation decisions remain open.
items.boundary: These are release-operation requirements rather than editor feature implementation.

items.name: Independent macOS interchange
items.current: The project formats and compatibility paths are documented, but independently reviewed macOS fixtures remain a planned qualification step.
items.boundary: Historical parity reports and self-generated round trips are not independent cross-platform proof.
